title: VPC core
oneLiner: A subnet is public only because of its route to an internet gateway. Security groups allow and remember replies; NACLs can deny and forget them. Gateway endpoints are free but only for S3 and DynamoDB, and only from inside the VPC.

notes.html: A VPC lives in one region, and each subnet lives in one AZ. What makes a subnet public is one route: 0.0.0.0/0 → internet gateway. Private subnets send that route to a NAT gateway, or have no internet route at all.

questions.q: EC2 instances in a private subnet must read objects from an S3 bucket in the same region. Traffic must not go over the internet, and the team wants the lowest cost. What should they use?

options.t: A NAT gateway in a public subnet
options.why: Works, but traffic leaves through the internet gateway and you pay per GB of NAT processing.

options.t: A gateway VPC endpoint for S3
options.why: Right. Free, a route-table entry, and traffic stays on the AWS network.

options.t: An interface VPC endpoint for S3
options.why: Works and is private, but you pay per hour and per GB. Gateway is the cheaper fit inside the VPC.

options.t: VPC peering with the S3 service VPC
options.why: There is no S3 VPC to peer with.

questions.q: An on-premises data center connects to a VPC over Direct Connect with a private VIF. Servers on-premises must upload to S3 over this private connection, without using public IPs. What should the architect add?

options.t: A gateway endpoint for S3 in the VPC
options.why: Gateway endpoints are route-table entries inside the VPC. Traffic arriving from on-premises can't use them.

options.t: An interface endpoint for S3 in the VPC
options.why: Right. It has private IPs in your subnet, so on-premises can reach it over DX or VPN.

options.t: A NAT gateway in the VPC
options.why: NAT gives private subnets internet access. It doesn't help on-prem reach S3 privately.

options.t: S3 Transfer Acceleration
options.why: That speeds up uploads over the public internet. It isn't private.

questions.q: Which TWO services can use a gateway VPC endpoint?

options.t: Amazon S3
options.why: Right. One of only two.

options.t: Amazon SQS
options.why: SQS uses interface endpoints.

options.t: Amazon DynamoDB
options.why: Right. The other one.

options.t: AWS KMS
options.why: KMS uses interface endpoints.

options.t: AWS Systems Manager
options.why: SSM uses interface endpoints.

questions.q: Lambda functions in private subnets call SQS and KMS. Security now forbids any route to the internet, so the NAT gateway is being removed. What keeps the functions working?

options.t: Gateway endpoints for SQS and KMS
options.why: Gateway endpoints exist only for S3 and DynamoDB.

options.t: Interface endpoints for SQS and KMS
options.why: Right. Private IPs in the subnet, no internet route needed.

options.t: Move the functions out of the VPC
options.why: That would work technically, but it ignores why they're in the VPC (they likely reach private resources).

options.t: An egress-only internet gateway
options.why: That's still internet access, and it's IPv6 only.

questions.q: A three-tier app has an ALB, EC2 app servers in an Auto Scaling group, and RDS MySQL. The DB must accept connections only from the app servers, even as instances scale in and out. How should the DB's security group be set?

options.t: Allow 3306 from the private subnet CIDR
options.why: Too broad: anything in that subnet, not just app servers, gets in.

options.t: Allow 3306 from the app tier's security group
options.why: Right. Security group chaining: any instance in the app SG is allowed, whatever its IP.

options.t: Allow 3306 from each app server's private IP
options.why: Breaks as soon as the ASG replaces an instance.

options.t: Add a NACL rule allowing 3306 from the ALB
options.why: The ALB doesn't connect to the DB, and NACLs work on IP ranges, not tiers.

questions.q: Web servers behind an ALB currently allow port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0. The team wants them reachable only through the ALB. What is the most secure change?

options.t: Allow port 80 only from the ALB's security group
options.why: Right. Only traffic coming from the ALB's ENIs is accepted.

options.t: Allow port 80 from the ALB's public IP addresses
options.why: ALB IPs change over time, and traffic from the ALB uses its private IPs.

options.t: Add a NACL that denies 0.0.0.0/0
options.why: That would also block the ALB, and the replies.

options.t: Move the web servers to a public subnet
options.why: That makes them more exposed, not less.

questions.q: Logs show attacks from one IP address against a public web app in a subnet. The team must block that IP right away. What should they use?

options.t: A deny rule in the security group
options.why: Security groups have no deny rules.

options.t: A deny rule in the subnet's network ACL
options.why: Right. NACLs can deny a specific IP or range.

options.t: Remove the route to the internet gateway
options.why: That takes the whole site offline.

options.t: VPC Flow Logs
options.why: Flow Logs record traffic. They don't block anything.

questions.q: An engineer creates a new custom network ACL and associates it with a subnet. Immediately, all traffic to the subnet stops. Why?

options.t: Custom NACLs deny all inbound and outbound traffic until you add rules
options.why: Right. Only the default NACL allows everything.

options.t: NACLs are stateful and need an outbound rule
options.why: NACLs are stateless, and that's not why everything stopped.

options.t: Security groups were reset
options.why: Associating a NACL doesn't touch security groups.

options.t: The subnet lost its route table
options.why: Associating a NACL doesn't change routes.

questions.q: A NACL allows inbound TCP 443 from 0.0.0.0/0 and has an outbound rule allowing only TCP 443. Clients can't load the site. What is missing?

options.t: An inbound rule for ephemeral ports
options.why: Inbound is fine. The responses are what's failing.

options.t: An outbound rule for ephemeral ports 1024-65535
options.why: Right. NACLs are stateless, so responses to clients' high ports need their own allow rule.

options.t: A security group outbound rule
options.why: Security groups are stateful. Replies are allowed automatically.

options.t: A route to the NAT gateway
options.why: This is a public site reached through the internet gateway.

questions.q: Instances in private subnets across three AZs use one NAT gateway in AZ-a. When AZ-a has an outage, all instances lose internet access. What fixes this with the least management?

options.t: Replace it with a NAT instance in an Auto Scaling group
options.why: More work to run, and it's the old approach.

options.t: Create a NAT gateway in each AZ and point each private subnet's route to the NAT in its own AZ
options.why: Right. A NAT gateway is redundant within its AZ only.

options.t: Put the NAT gateway in a private subnet
options.why: A NAT gateway must sit in a public subnet.

options.t: Add a second internet gateway
options.why: A VPC has only one internet gateway, and that's not the single point of failure here.

questions.q: A company needs IPv6-enabled instances in a private subnet to reach the internet for updates, while blocking inbound IPv6 connections from the internet. What should they use?

options.t: NAT gateway
options.why: NAT gateways are for IPv4.

options.t: Egress-only internet gateway
options.why: Right. Outbound-only for IPv6.

options.t: Internet gateway with a security group
options.why: That would let the instances be reachable if they had inbound rules. Egress-only is the purpose-built answer.

options.t: Gateway VPC endpoint
options.why: Endpoints are for AWS services, not the internet.

questions.q: Administrators need shell access to EC2 instances in private subnets. Security wants no inbound ports open, no bastion hosts and no SSH keys, with sessions logged. What should they use?

options.t: A bastion host in a public subnet
options.why: Needs port 22 open and keys to manage.

options.t: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager
options.why: Right. Agent-based, no inbound ports, sessions logged to S3 or CloudWatch.

options.t: EC2 Instance Connect over the internet
options.why: Still needs port 22 reachable.

options.t: A site-to-site VPN
options.why: Adds a network path but still needs SSH and keys.

questions.q: VPC A is peered with VPC B, and VPC B is peered with VPC C. Instances in A can't reach C. What is the reason?

options.t: Peering is not transitive
options.why: Right. A needs its own peering with C, or use a Transit Gateway.

options.t: The security groups block it
options.why: Possible in general, but the core rule here is that peering doesn't pass traffic through B.

options.t: Peering only works within one account
options.why: Peering works across accounts and regions.

options.t: The CIDRs overlap
options.why: Nothing says they overlap. If they did, the peering couldn't be created.

questions.q: A company has 60 VPCs across several accounts and a VPN to its data center. They want any VPC to reach any other VPC and on-premises, with central routing control. What is the most scalable design?

options.t: Full mesh of VPC peering connections
options.why: Around 1,770 peering connections, each with routes. Doesn't scale.

options.t: A Transit Gateway with all VPCs and the VPN attached
options.why: Right. Hub and spoke, transitive, route tables control who talks to whom.

options.t: PrivateLink between all VPCs
options.why: PrivateLink exposes single services, not whole networks.

options.t: One VGW per VPC with its own VPN
options.why: 60 VPNs to manage, and VPC-to-VPC still isn't solved.

questions.q: A SaaS provider wants to expose an API to hundreds of customer VPCs. Many customers use the same CIDR range as the provider. Traffic must stay off the internet. What should the provider use?

options.t: VPC peering with each customer
options.why: Overlapping CIDRs block peering, and hundreds of peerings don't scale.

options.t: Transit Gateway shared to all customers
options.why: Overlapping CIDRs are a problem there too, and it opens whole networks.

options.t: PrivateLink: an endpoint service behind an NLB, with interface endpoints in customer VPCs
options.why: Right. One service, one direction, overlapping CIDRs don't matter.

options.t: A public API Gateway
options.why: That goes over the internet.

questions.q: A subnet uses 10.0.1.0/24. How many IP addresses can be assigned to instances?

options.why: That's the total. AWS reserves 5.
That's the usual on-prem answer. AWS reserves 5, not 2.
Right. 256 minus 5 reserved.
AWS reserves 5, not 6.

questions.q: A security team must find out why connections from one IP to a database are being rejected. They need records of accepted and rejected traffic, not packet contents. What should they enable?

options.t: VPC Flow Logs
options.why: Right. Source, destination, port and ACCEPT/REJECT for each flow.

options.t: Traffic Mirroring
options.why: Copies packet contents. More than needed and more expensive.

options.t: CloudTrail
options.why: Records API calls, not network traffic.

options.t: AWS Config
options.why: Records resource configuration changes, not traffic.

questions.q: A company must inspect all outbound traffic from its VPCs and allow only approved domain names, using a managed AWS service. What should they deploy?

options.t: Security groups with domain rules
options.why: Security groups work with IPs, ports and SG references, not domain names.

options.t: AWS Network Firewall
options.why: Right. Managed stateful firewall with domain allow-lists.

options.t: AWS WAF on the NAT gateway
options.why: WAF attaches to HTTP services like ALB and CloudFront, not NAT gateways.

options.t: Network ACLs
options.why: NACLs filter IP ranges and ports, not domains.

questions.q: A bucket policy must make sure objects can only be read through a specific VPC endpoint. Which condition key should it use?

options.t: aws:SourceIp
options.why: Traffic through a VPC endpoint uses private IPs, so source IP conditions don't fit.

options.t: aws:SourceVpce
options.why: Right. Deny unless the request came through that endpoint ID.

options.t: aws:PrincipalOrgID
options.why: Limits by AWS Organization, not network path.

options.t: s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption
options.why: That's about encryption headers.

questions.q: A VPC with a /24 CIDR is running out of IP addresses for new subnets. What is the least disruptive fix?

options.t: Create a new, larger VPC and migrate
options.why: Works but is very disruptive.

options.t: Add a secondary CIDR block to the VPC
options.why: Right. Then create new subnets in the new range.

options.t: Resize the existing subnets
options.why: Subnet CIDRs can't be changed after creation.

options.t: Use a NAT gateway to share addresses
options.why: NAT doesn't create addresses for instances.
